article.heading: Nutrient Dense Soft Pastilles increase Gut Brain Axis (GBA) Functionality
article.metaAnalysis: > Synopsis (based on product trials since 2023 and literature review of 19 reference sites)
article.paragraph1: The gut and the brain communicate bidirectionally through the Gut–Brain Axis (GBA), which operates through interconnected neural, endocrine, immune, and microbiome pathways. Emerging evidence shows that dietary choices, spring water and exposure to Schumann resonance (grounding) can influence these pathways and modulate gut–brain communication. Lifestyle activities align with stress-reduction and nervous-system calming mechanisms indirectly support GBA regulation.
article.paragraph3: Functional food and progressive clinical nutrition made save, simple and effective.
article.paragraph4: The certified organic ingredients are Halal Gelatine (source chicken, sheep, fish, bovine), Annona, Plantain, Gum Arabica, Roselle, Beetroot, Amla, Virgin Coconut Oil, Nipah Nectar, Panela (raw cane sugar)
article.paragraph5: Nutrient-dense soft pastilles containing resistant starch (paleo prebiotics), phytosterols, omega-3 and MCTs, polyphenols (antioxidants), pro-collagen complex (amino acids, polypeptides, glycoproteins and ascorbate) together with essential vitamins and minerals, support the GBA interventions.
article.paragraph6: When formulated with certified organic bioactive ingredients, soft pastilles may provide a safe, convenient, and well-tolerated modality for supporting GBA functionality. By delivering phytonutrients, bioactive compounds and medical grade probiotics we influence microbial diversity, short-chain fatty acid synthesis, enhance mitochondrial activity, regulate inflammatory signalling and neurotransmitter biosynthesis.
article.paragraph7: Soft Pastilles are formulated for maximum quick absorption via the buccal sublingual pathway thus giving early results.
article.productDescription: Soft pastille formulations can help stabilize neurocognitive and autonomic responses. Improved GBA responses can enhance emotional resilience, cognitive processing and stress tolerance, thereby increasing patient receptiveness and engagement in mental-health counselling and related psychotherapeutic interventions.
article.resistantStarchContent: feeds beneficial gut bacteria (commensal microbes). These probiotics ferment this fiber into beneficial metabolites, notably short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), which improves intestinal barrier function, reduce systemic and neuro inflammation.
article.omega3Content: play essential roles in cellular energy metabolism, neurodevelopment and cognitive processing. These healthy lipids support the synthesis of neuronal membranes, enhance mitochondrial efficiency and facilitate the production of ketone bodies associated with improved mood regulation and a reduced risk of depressive symptoms.
article.omega3Content2: These lipids been studied for their capacity to modulate cholesterol profile by increasing HDL cholesterol, balancing the Omega 3:6 ratio and dietary trans-fat burden.
article.vitaminsContent: Ascorbate, B vitamins, folate, zinc, and magnesium are involved as coenzymes and cofactors in the metabolic pathways that affect the development and functioning of the nervous system and neuro hormones
article.probioticsContent: When paired with nutrient-rich soft pastilles, as reported in several probiotic–nutrition synergy studies, these med-grade probiotics supports clearer focus, calmer mood, and healthier digestion. Research in children shows benefits in strengthening natural immunity and easing seasonal flu-like or allergy-related discomfort.

article.oralHygieneTitle: Oral Hygiene and Early Dental Care
article.oralHygieneContent: "Buccal/sublingual nutrient-dense pastilles direct delivery beneficial probiotics, natural anti-inflammatory compounds, prebiotic substrates, phytonutrients (cofactors/vitamins/coenzyme) into the biofilm environment where they can compete with pathogens, produce antimicrobial metabolites, modulate local immunity, and change local pH. This may help modulate the oral microbiome and mucosal health.
article.oralHygieneContent2: Evidence from clinical trials of lozenges with probiotics and bioactive ingredients shows improvements in some markers of oral dysbiosis and gum inflammation. Results are promising but heterogeneous. Systemic nutritional effects depend on absorption and is dose dependent.
article.oralHygieneContent3: These interventions should be considered adjunctive and not replacements for professional dental care."
article.mechanismContent: NVC nutrient-dense soft pastille may function as a cofactor and coenzyme delivery system, that support microcapillary functionality, cellular metabolism, anti-inflammatory activity and microbiome stability. The formulation can act in line with "psychobiotic" principles thus contributing in some parts to improved physiological balance, better stress modulation and complementary support to well-being. While not a replacement for medical therapy, functional soft pastilles facilitate 'nutrient synergy' that enhance the body's response to prescription medication and promote treatment efficacy in the elderly.
article.researchContent: Certified organic cultivation of selected non-GMO plant species has been shown to yield higher concentrations of key bioactive compounds, including Acetogenins and Thymoquinone, presently under investigation for their potent anti-inflammatory, immunomodulatory, and cytoprotective properties. Our cultivation and processing activities at the Agri Research Institute operate under a strict Farm to Pharmacy framework, ensuring traceability, phytochemical integrity and therapeutic consistency across all research batches and clinical-grade formulations.

science.intro: Gut-Brain Axis [GBA] refers to the bidirectional neural signalling pathway between the brain, nerves, stomach, colon, hormones, immune system and gut microbes. This 'second brain' is generally referred to as source of emotional intelligence, supporting social norms, learning focus, restful sleep and wellbeing.
science.functionality: This functionality is influenced by prebiotics, probiotics, oral hygiene, human intestinal microbes, nutrient synergy and metabolic chemistry. These complex microbes ~ molecules ~ mitochondria co-dependency provide the important teamwork necessary for appetite regulation, nutrition absorption, bowel movement, hormone production, neurological functions, stress coping and immune response.
science.studies: Numerous studies show that emotional wellbeing, mood modulation, movement coordination, learning development and social skills are inherited, initiated and regulated by our friendly commensal gut bacteria acquired during birth and adolescence.
science.researchContent: Clinical researchers Dr Nobuyuki Sudo and Dr Yoichi Chida of Psychosomatic Medicine at Kyushu University contributed to the discovery of the gut-brain axis through a 2004 study.
science.nagoyaStudy: Scientist at the Nagoya University Graduate School of Medicine in Japan conducted a meta-analysis of stool samples collected from patients in Japan, Taiwan, China, Germany, and the U.S. that suffer from varied neurological conditions. The research team sequenced all the genetic material in the stool samples, examining both the genetic and microbial makeup of the stool. This 2024 research exploring the relationship between the gut and the brain showed evidence that the happy colony of microbes, influences cognitive development and emotional wellbeing.
science.dysbiosisContent: Gut Dysbiosis disrupts this happiness and causes heighten inflammation, which is linked to neurodegenerative conditions and indigestion, food intolerance, bloating, malabsorption, constipation and IBS.
science.quote: "Emerging research continues to show that dietary patterns, digestive efficacy, nutrient assimilation and neurochemical balance are interconnected. Gut-Brain Axis significantly influences metabolic regulation, cognitive development, stress coping and emotional stability,"
science.treatmentContent: Practical treatment protocols to restore Gut-Brain Axis functionality must be a slow-steady–safe approach. Safe therapies include gelatine or pectin base infused with phytonutrient, paleo prebiotics meals, vegan ketogenic diets, psychobiotics or life-culture med-grade probiotics and anti-inflammatory polyphenols.
science.specialNeedsContent: Special Needs Educators or ASD Therapists or Paediatricians in teaching hospitals are well-placed to validate the efficacy of long-term treatment plans for children with ADHD and students with learning difficulties by conducting structured before-and-after evaluations of attentiveness, engagement, receptiveness scores and academic progress.

science.communitySubtitle: Nutritional Care and Learning Development in Neurodivergent Children
science.communityContent1: Children with ASD and ADHD commonly struggle with more than attention, learning and social skills; many neurodivergent children experience sensitive digestion, limited food preference, food intolerance, excessive sugar cravings, restless sleep and challenges in managing emotions.
science.communityContent2: Today, medical researchers understand far more clearly that the gut and brain are deeply connected through food chemistry, nutrient synergy, neural pathways, immune messengers, hormones and the activity of gut microbes.
science.communityContent3: This relationship called the Gut–Brain Axis plays an important role in behaviour, mood, and how neurodivergent children think, feel, and learn.
science.communityContent4: This community outreach talk introduces parents to practical, science-informed strategies that support their child's wellbeing through gentle improvements in gut health. The session explains, in simple language, how gut bacteria influence mood, focus, stress response, and sleep quality; why digestive problems are common in neurodivergent children; and how diet, daily routines, and lifestyle habits can positively affect behaviour and attention.
science.communityContent5: Parents will learn safe and achievable interventions such as using gut-friendly foods, prebiotics and probiotics, reducing common dietary triggers, improving sleep hygiene, encouraging movement, and creating a calmer sensory environment. The talk emphasises that gut-brain support is not a cure, but a complementary approach that can enhance therapy outcomes and improve daily functioning. By the end of the session, parents will gain actionable steps they can start at home, renewed confidence in supporting their child's development, and a realistic understanding of how nurturing gut health can contribute to better behaviour, emotional balance, and overall quality of life for children with ASD and ADHD.
